name: era-current-peer-keeps-modern-content
description: a current peer gets no era shim at all: modern content and subagent attribution reach it untouched, the subagent lifecycle reaches the consumer, and a retired part is refused by outgoing enforcement rather than quietly upgraded
kill: make the 0.0.39, 0.0.47 or 0.0.57 era shim install unconditionally (drop its compareVersions gate). Each has material of its own here: 0.0.39 flattens the first message's parts to a bare string, 0.0.47 rewrites the second message's retired {type:binary} part into a media part instead of letting enforcement refuse it (so both the request and the warning change), and 0.0.57 strips subagentRunId from the third message as well as dropping the SUBAGENT_* events. The 0.0.45 gate is NOT covered by this fixture, or by any other: that shim only translates THINKING_* events, and the always-on CompatibilityBoundary runs innermost and converts every one of them before a version-gated shim can see it, so installing 0.0.45 unconditionally is a no-op on every possible stream

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client has no era shims to gate, so nothing here can be transformed by one and the request it builds comes straight from the fixture input. It also handles the retired part differently and earlier: AGUIMessageJsonConverter's closed input-content union rejects {"type":"binary"} while the run input is being deserialized, so the WHOLE second message is left out before the run starts (see era-0-0-47) rather than being emptied by outgoing enforcement, and that rejection is recorded as unrepresentable input rather than raised as a warning. `warnings` is emptied only to displace the base expectation, since an override replaces a key rather than removing it; `noWarnings` is what asserts this lane's silence. The request assertion is reduced to the run identity for the same reason era-0-0-47's is. What still holds here, and is what this fixture is for on this lane, is that the SUBAGENT_* lifecycle reaches the consumer as ordinary 1.0 events, in order, alongside the run terminals.
